newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, brace for more possible floods.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, brace for more possible floods.

text.p: Polish shares fell after a two-day day gain and analysts said investors over the weekend would be watching to what degree current rain around the country could lead to this month's second flood wave.
Heavy rains already fell on Western Poland on Friday morning, including areas already hit by flooding, but not all weather forecasters were pessimistic.

"The flooding has an unclear affect on the macroeconomy, whether we're talking about the first or second (possible) wave and doesn't encourage investment decisions....It seems players are at least holding back," said Bogdan Duszek of PKO BP house.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.4 percent to 15,348.9 points and turnover fell 13.1 percent to 180.9 million zlotys ($51.9 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 50 to 32 with 24 stocks flat.

Analysts said construction and furniture firms could benefit from flood reconstruction, such as builder Mostostal Warszawa, up 7.2 percent in light trade on Friday after three other Mostostals gained big on Thursday.

They said Kredyt Bank, up 9.1 percent in light trade, benefited from Thursday's news its shareholders approved a merger with Polish Investment Bank (PBI) in which Kredyt's number of shares would not rise.
